🌍 YOUNG PEOPLE ARE NOT WAITING FOR THE ENERGY TRANSITION. THEY ARE ALREADY SHAPING IT.
 
As #UNGA81 gathers momentum, young people should not be discussed only as the generation that will inherit the energy transition.
 
They are already part of it.
 
👥 Over the next decade, 1.2 billion young people in developing countries will reach working age. Yet only around 420 million jobs are projected to be created.
 
⚡ At the same time, the energy transition is opening new economic opportunities. Renewable energy already supports 16.6 million jobs worldwide.
 
🎓 But there is a skills gap. Globally, only 1 in 20 Gen Z workers has the green skills needed for the changing economy, compared with 1 in 8 workers overall.
 
💡 This is not simply a jobs challenge. It is a youth opportunity challenge.
 
Young people are already developing ideas, building businesses, learning new technologies and creating solutions in their communities.
 
But meaningful participation requires more than asking for their views.
 
It means giving young people the skills and practical experience to turn ideas into action. Access to mentors, networks and finance. Opportunities to build businesses and careers. And a real voice in the decisions shaping the energy systems they will live with for decades.
 
Young people should not simply inherit the energy transition.
 
They should have the opportunity to build it.
 
As UNGA81’s High-Level Week approaches, we will continue bringing young people’s perspectives into the energy conversation in New York — and exploring how we can better connect their ambition and ideas with real opportunities.
 
The next generation is ready.
 
The question is whether the opportunities will be ready for them.

#UNGA81 #YouthInEnergy #EnergyForDevelopment #SDG7
